read_by: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and release decision
input: Freshwater flood depth above substation grade (ft), 0 to 10 ft; or water-surface and grade elevations (m) on the same vertical datum
not_covered: GSU parts as separate units: switchgear, main transformer, transformer auxiliaries and controls, protection and SCADA, station service and DC, cable terminations (withheld, not zero)
Turbine-base electrical and pad or turbine step-up transformers (withheld)
Turbine foundation (needs a separate scour and erosion pathway) and civil access and drainage (needs a split)
Elevated turbine equipment: rotor, nacelle, tower (geometry-screened, not declared zero)
Fieldwork and transport support (allocated once after repair scope; no fragility)
out_of_scope: Outage restoration, business interruption, curtailment, revenue and insurance
Soft, sunk and non-physical costs (excluded from the physical base)
Other hazards in the same event (tropical-cyclone wind, tornado); one event must not charge the same value twice
missing_mechanisms: Scour, erosion, saturated-soil support loss, debris impact and wave loading
Flood duration (captured but has no effect on the result)

how_to_use.share_of: Full direct replacement value of the same facility-level GSU/substation (not project TIV, not the mixed 72 USD/kW electrical row)

outputs.single_event: conditional: exact Hazus substation class, the Hazus 2.1 Table 7.9 assumption set, freshwater non-contaminated water, depth 0 to 10 ft
outputs.scenario_dollars: conditional: only with an explicit same-substation replacement value and exposure fraction
outputs.yearly_loss: withheld for this partial screening release (consumer-owned)

conditions: substation_hazus_class must be ESSL, ESSM or ESSH (all three use the same points)
Salt, brackish, contaminated or unknown water withholds
Depth must be unprotected or internal post-bypass depth; no extra mitigation credit
Negative depth rejects, depth above 10 ft withholds, missing depth rejects (never treated as dry)
One shared substation is counted once, never repeated by turbine count or across solar and wind
The cell gives no covered value share; the substation value must come from the site

method.summary: FEMA Hazus-MH 2.1 Table 7.9 whole-substation depth-damage table used exactly as published (0 to 10 ft, damage 0 to 0.15), linear between one-foot points

key_sources: FEMA, Hazus-MH Flood Model Technical Manual 2.1, Table 7.9 (FW-S011)
FEMA, Hazus 7.0 Flood Technical Manual (2025), electric-power status (FW-S012)
USACE, HEC-FIA Technical Reference, depth-percent damage relationships (FW-S006)
NEMA GD 1-2016, Evaluating Water-Damaged Electrical Equipment (FW-S002; historical context)
NREL, Cost of Wind Energy Review 2024 (FW-S008; value anatomy only)
judgment: Only freshwater non-contaminated water gets a number; all other water types withhold
No extension past 10 ft: deeper water withholds instead of holding the last value
Missing or incomplete depth is rejected, never read as dry
Flood duration is recorded but does not change the result
The whole-substation curve and any future component curves must never be charged together
Unknown ownership keeps the substation out of the baseline
open_items: Review of the 2026 NEMA successor guide (CS 70006-2026) is still open
Current Hazus 7.0 disables electric-power loss functions; the table is legacy and not claims-calibrated
Component-level GSU curves could replace the whole-substation curve later
Salt and contaminated water response not modelled

rows.variants: Hazus substation class ESSL, ESSM or ESSH (same points)
rows.shape_basis: Hazus 2.1 Table 7.9 points; official but legacy, no claims calibration
rows.cost_basis: Same Hazus table gives damage as a share of the substation's replacement value; denominator row T3

notes.text: Whole-substation unit; never charge it together with the GSU component parts
